note: The private VISUAL EVAL SET (docs/SPX_EXAMPLES_CORPUS.md workstream 4): real on-air frames from the licence-restricted spx_examples corpus, each paired with the template that produced it and with our own written observations. This file is the CURATION - paths, pairings, and what we saw, in our own words. The pictures themselves never enter the repo; `node scripts/spx-eval-set.mjs` assembles the reviewable page locally from the corpus plus the gallery's rendered hold frames. Observations describe what is visible in the frame. They are evidence for a taste decision, never a decision: where one contradicts docs/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md it is filed under `openQuestions` for the owner, exactly as the 2026-08-02 production deltas were.

entries.what: Flagship talk-show host strap, one line: the presenter's name over a full-width bottom band.
observations: The panel is a full-frame-width band, not a boxed strap: it runs edge to edge and fades out toward the right rather than ending at a corner.
No accent colour, no rule, no chip, no logo inside the graphic. The only mark on screen is the channel bug in the top-left corner, outside the strap entirely.
The name is set LIGHT, white, at a large size - hierarchy comes from size and position, never from weight or colour.
Text starts at roughly a tenth of the frame width in, well inside title-safe, and the band's own top edge is soft.

entries.what: The same strap carrying two lines: guest name plus their title.
observations: Identical band, identical left margin: the one-line and two-line variants are the same graphic with a line added, not two designs.
The name-to-title size step is modest - the title reads clearly as secondary but stays close in size.
Both lines share the same light weight and the same white. Nothing is bolded to rank it.
The band does not grow a keyline or a shadow to carry the second line; the scrim alone does the work.

entries.what: Guest introduction board: name and age as a heading, then three bulleted facts, over the left half of the frame.
observations: The scrim is a half-frame column with a soft right edge, so the guest stays visible in the other half - the composition is designed around the shot, not dropped on top of it.
Bullets are plain dots and only the first line of each item carries one; wrapped lines align to the text, not to the dot.
The gaps BETWEEN bullet items are far larger than the line spacing inside one, which is what makes three items read as three.
Line count per bullet varies (one, two, three lines) and the board simply grows downward - no fixed row height.

entries.what: Guest motto board: a label line, the quotation, and the guest's own signature as an image.
observations: Same half-frame scrim as the bio board - one shape serves the whole pack.
The label ('X's motto:') is the same size as the quotation, separated only by a blank line. Nothing is set small.
The quotation carries no quotation marks and no decorative typography; the signature at the bottom is the only graphic element.
The signature is a personal artefact rendered as an image, not a font - a reminder that a real pack ships per-item picture fields.

entries.what: Music-requests board: three guests, each with an artist and a song title, over a dark stage shot.
observations: Three repeating groups of three lines, with the guest name larger and the artist/song lines beneath at one size.
Each group is marked by a small decorative musical-stave glyph in the margin - the only ornament anywhere in the pack, and it sits OUTSIDE the text column.
The block is left-aligned in the left third with a very generous gap between groups.
No scrim is visible here because the underlying shot is already near-black - the design relies on the picture, which is exactly the case our legibility floor exists for.

entries.what: End credits rolling over the closing shot.
observations: Centred single column - the one graphic in the pack that centres, and it centres because a credit roll genuinely is symmetric.
Role heading then names underneath at the same size and weight, with a full blank line between groups doing all the grouping.
No scrim at all: white type straight onto a bright daytime exterior, and legibility is carried by the type's size alone.
CAVEAT: this frame is a capture of a streaming player, so the scrubber and player controls along the bottom are not part of the graphic.

openQuestions: Every name line in this pack is set LIGHT, while docs/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md §1 asks for weight 600-800 on a name. Six frames from one flagship production are not a mandate to change the guardrail, but they are evidence that a light large name is professional broadcast rather than a mistake. Owner call, like the 2026-08-02 production deltas.
The name-to-title size ratio in the guest strap reads well under DESIGN_LANGUAGE's 1.8-2.2:1, with the difference carried by position instead. Same status: observed, not ratified.

Nothing in this pack uses an accent colour. Our catalog treats one accent as the house signature; this production treats zero accent as the house signature. Worth knowing before a knowledge card claims an accent is required.

ownerPicks.note: Which RENDERED corpus frames belong in the taste-calibration set is a taste judgement, so the list is deliberately empty rather than guessed by an agent. Fill it with ids from spx-corpus-out/gallery/index.html; the assembler will include them beside the on-air pairs above.
